world.title: Iran warns new war could outlast previous conflict as Trump weighs strikes
world.summary: Iran warned that renewed fighting with the United States could last longer than the previous conflict after President Donald Trump said U.S. forces still had one or two targets to hit, including the suspected underground nuclear complex at Pickaxe Mountain. Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said Trump would not
world.content: Iran warned that renewed fighting with the United States could last longer than the previous conflict after President Donald Trump said U.S. forces still had one or two targets to hit, including the suspected underground nuclear complex at Pickaxe Mountain. Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said Trump would not dictate the timing or terms of any war’s end. Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei said he had received a letter from U.S. Vice President JD Vance seeking to revive talks, while Iranian negotiators met Qatari mediators in Doha. Tehran says it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz or negotiate unless Washington unfreezes Iranian assets, ends its naval blockade of Iranian ports, lifts sanctions and ends the war on all fronts. Trump has not announced a decision on further strikes. He discussed Iran with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday; reports cited by France 24 said Netanyahu favored striking after the U.S. midterm elections on Tuesday, while Trump wanted talks to continue. Reports said renewed military action could begin as early as Nov. 4.
world.image_alt: Iran warns new war could outlast previous conflict as Trump weighs strikes

world.title: France opens attempted murder probe after Paris petrol-bomb attack
world.summary: French prosecutors opened an attempted-murder investigation on Nov. 1 after an incendiary device struck security forces during protests in Paris, setting a gendarme’s protective clothing alight. Prosecutors said explosives were thrown at about 15 gendarmes and police officers. Reported injuries included second-degree b
world.content: French prosecutors opened an attempted-murder investigation on Nov. 1 after an incendiary device struck security forces during protests in Paris, setting a gendarme’s protective clothing alight. Prosecutors said explosives were thrown at about 15 gendarmes and police officers. Reported injuries included second-degree burns, and 13 members of the gendarme’s unit were injured. The attack occurred near Porte de Charenton, where the march ended. The clashes occurred on the third consecutive weekend of demonstrations over living costs, public services and other government policies. France’s Interior Ministry counted 320,000 participants nationwide, while organizers estimated nearly 500,000. The ministry reported 779 arrests during the protests and Halloween night, as well as 159 law-enforcement officers injured. No one had been arrested in connection with the firebomb attack, and investigators were working to identify those responsible. Student groups planned further school and university blockades on Tuesday and Thursday, followed by a demonstration by workers and unions on Nov. 5.
world.image_alt: France opens attempted murder probe after Paris petrol-bomb attack

world.title: UN ends Western Sahara peacekeeping mission after Security Council deadlock
world.summary: The United Nations’ 35-year peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, known as MINURSO, began winding down on Nov. 1 after the Security Council failed to renew its mandate, leaving the territory without the mission’s ceasefire monitoring. Russia vetoed a U.S.-backed draft on Oct. 30, and a competing Russian proposal to e
world.content: The United Nations’ 35-year peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, known as MINURSO, began winding down on Nov. 1 after the Security Council failed to renew its mandate, leaving the territory without the mission’s ceasefire monitoring. Russia vetoed a U.S.-backed draft on Oct. 30, and a competing Russian proposal to extend the mission also failed. Its mandate expired at midnight on Oct. 31. MINURSO was created in 1991 to monitor a ceasefire and prepare a referendum on self-determination. The vote never took place because Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front disagreed over who could vote. Morocco welcomed the decision not to renew the mission, while the Polisario and Algeria objected to the outcome and the U.S. draft. The UN says a smaller team will oversee the return or disposal of mission equipment, while its political work will continue through envoy Staffan de Mistura.
world.image_alt: UN ends Western Sahara peacekeeping mission after Security Council deadlock

world.title: India opposition leader vows legal action against Modi over voter rolls
world.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said at a New Delhi rally on Sunday that the opposition would pursue legal action against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah after demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s removal. Gandhi alleged “vote theft”; the opposition says the voter-roll changes cou
world.content: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said at a New Delhi rally on Sunday that the opposition would pursue legal action against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah after demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s removal. Gandhi alleged “vote theft”; the opposition says the voter-roll changes could benefit Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), while the BJP and Election Commission deny wrongdoing. The voter-roll review, known as the Special Intensive Revision, has removed more than 130 million names from draft electoral rolls. Opposition parties say the review has disproportionately affected eligible voters, particularly Muslims and other minorities. Election officials say it targets duplicate, deceased and otherwise ineligible registrations, and that wrongly excluded voters can seek reinstatement. The dispute intensified after a report said two election commissioners had raised internal concerns about the revision, registration procedures and digital systems. Tens of thousands attended Sunday’s rally, where senior Congress and regional opposition figures joined Gandhi. Senior BJP leaders denounced the protest, while the Election Commission defended the process. The next general election is due in 2029, and the opposition says it will continue pressing for Kumar’s resignation.
world.image_alt: India opposition leader vows legal action against Modi over voter rolls

world.title: Israel’s election chief says fraud probe will not overturn results
world.summary: Israel’s election chief said Sunday, Nov. 1, that an investigation into suspected foreign interference would not overturn last week’s parliamentary vote, even if the allegations are confirmed. Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, chairman of the Central Elections Committee, said the election was conducted properly and
world.content: Israel’s election chief said Sunday, Nov. 1, that an investigation into suspected foreign interference would not overturn last week’s parliamentary vote, even if the allegations are confirmed. Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, chairman of the Central Elections Committee, said the election was conducted properly and the results reflected voters’ choices. The Shin Bet, Israel’s internal security agency, is investigating whether Qatar funded Ra’am, an Arab-led party. Both Ra’am and Qatar deny the allegation. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud bloc won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, Israel’s parliament, while the opposition bloc led by Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot won 48. Arab-led parties Ra’am and the Joint List won 19 seats combined, leaving neither main bloc with the 61 needed for a majority. Together, the opposition and Arab parties could command 67 seats if they agree to cooperate. The investigation is continuing, and Sohlberg said suspicions were not proof. The election results are due to be certified this week, and President Isaac Herzog is scheduled to begin consultations with elected parties on Wednesday, Nov. 4. The new Knesset is due to be sworn in next week, followed by coalition negotiations.
world.image_alt: Israel’s election chief says fraud probe will not overturn results

world.title: Zelensky offers monthlong refinery pause for US Patriot missiles
world.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Nov. 1 that Ukraine would stop striking Russian oil refineries for a month if the United States supplied Patriot air-defense missiles for the same period. He also said Kyiv could halt the attacks if Russia stopped targeting Ukraine’s energy system, responding to President Don
world.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Nov. 1 that Ukraine would stop striking Russian oil refineries for a month if the United States supplied Patriot air-defense missiles for the same period. He also said Kyiv could halt the attacks if Russia stopped targeting Ukraine’s energy system, responding to President Donald Trump’s demand that both countries stop attacking energy facilities. The Trump administration approved a potential $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine on Oct. 30, but Zelensky warned deliveries could take years. Ukrainian officials have warned that their missile stocks are dwindling, and Zelensky has urged allies to transfer missiles from their own stockpiles while awaiting the new order. Trump has linked his push for an energy-site truce to rising energy prices, while Russian attacks have damaged Ukrainian power infrastructure. US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine are expected to resume this month after being effectively frozen since February, when the United States and Israel began strikes on Iran.
world.image_alt: Zelensky offers monthlong refinery pause for US Patriot missiles

world.title: Youth protests over costs spread across Europe as German rallies turn violent
world.summary: Youth-led demonstrations over living costs, education, housing and public services drew crowds across Europe on Saturday, with violence breaking out after rallies in several German cities. Organizers of Germany’s “Gen Z regelt” movement estimated 120,000 participants across more than 30 cities. Most marches were peacef
world.content: Youth-led demonstrations over living costs, education, housing and public services drew crowds across Europe on Saturday, with violence breaking out after rallies in several German cities. Organizers of Germany’s “Gen Z regelt” movement estimated 120,000 participants across more than 30 cities. Most marches were peaceful, but looting, fires and clashes with police followed rallies in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg. In Frankfurt, authorities reported at least 54 arrests and more than 100 injured police officers. France’s third consecutive weekend of protests drew an estimated 320,000 people, including 70,000 in Paris, according to the Interior Ministry; police made 779 arrests nationwide. Demonstrations also took place in Portugal, where police cleared a tent camp in Lisbon after a housing protest, and in Zurich, where police said rioters set vehicles and barricades alight. Participants in Germany also opposed spending cuts and plans to revive compulsory military service. Organizers rejected violence, while German officials blamed extremist groups and called for penalties against those involved. Gen Z regelt has called for another demonstration on Nov. 14; a separate Europe-wide protest is planned for Nov. 20.
world.image_alt: Youth protests over costs spread across Europe as German rallies turn violent

world.title: Binance customers withdraw $3.64 billion as exchange reopens after hack
world.summary: Customers withdrew a net $3.64 billion from Binance on Sunday, Nov. 1, after the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange began restoring transactions following a $6.3 billion theft. The FBI has blamed North Korea-linked hacking group TraderTraitor for the breach; Binance said it processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals
world.content: Customers withdrew a net $3.64 billion from Binance on Sunday, Nov. 1, after the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange began restoring transactions following a $6.3 billion theft. The FBI has blamed North Korea-linked hacking group TraderTraitor for the breach; Binance said it processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits during the first nine and a half hours after reopening. The net outflow represented about 2.1% of Binance’s $171 billion in assets under management, according to the exchange, which said withdrawals eased after an initial surge and deposits remained substantial. Binance says it has replaced about 95% of the stolen assets using company funds, its customer-protection reserve and its futures insurance fund. It says the remaining tokens are less liquid and may take longer to source. The exchange is restoring access in stages as it checks networks and assets. A full report on its investigation was expected Monday, Nov. 2.
world.image_alt: Binance customers withdraw $3.64 billion as exchange reopens after hack

Chief Executive Anthony Miller said the economic outlook was uncertain. Westpac New Zealand’s net profit fell 9% to NZ$1.087 billion as intense competi
business.content: Westpac Banking Corp. reported Australian net income of A$6.8 billion for the year ended September, down about 1% and below analysts’ average estimate of A$6.9 billion. Chief Executive Anthony Miller said the economic outlook was uncertain. Westpac New Zealand’s net profit fell 9% to NZ$1.087 billion as intense competition and narrower interest margins weighed on results. Its margin declined to 2.23% from 2.32% a year earlier. The bank also recorded a NZ$33 million impairment charge, compared with a NZ$44 million impairment benefit in the previous year.

business.title: Economist says Fed is managing Treasury yields as debt costs surge
business.summary: Robin Brooks, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, argues that Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is prioritizing management of long-term Treasury yields over the usual hawk-versus-dove debate on inflation. U.S. gross debt exceeds $40 trillion, and federal interest costs topped $1 trillion in fiscal 2026, excee
business.content: Robin Brooks, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, argues that Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is prioritizing management of long-term Treasury yields over the usual hawk-versus-dove debate on inflation. U.S. gross debt exceeds $40 trillion, and federal interest costs topped $1 trillion in fiscal 2026, exceeding defense spending. A Congressional Budget Office scenario with yields 1.5 percentage points above its 4.3% baseline projects $4.9 trillion in additional net interest costs over 10 years and publicly held debt reaching 133% of gross domestic product by 2036. John Sheehan, a portfolio manager at Osterweis Capital Management, said continued borrowing by governments and AI companies could put upward pressure on yields and leave some high-yield issuers unable to meet their obligations.
business.image_alt: Economist says Fed is managing Treasury yields as debt costs surge

business.title: Xiaomi tops 50,000 electric-car deliveries in October, still trails target
business.summary: Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi delivered more than 50,000 electric cars in October, its highest monthly total this year, as it expands production and its vehicle lineup. The company delivered about 336,000 cars in the first 10 months of 2026, roughly 61% of its 550,000-vehicle goal for the year. Xiaomi needs to delive
business.content: Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi delivered more than 50,000 electric cars in October, its highest monthly total this year, as it expands production and its vehicle lineup. The company delivered about 336,000 cars in the first 10 months of 2026, roughly 61% of its 550,000-vehicle goal for the year. Xiaomi needs to deliver about 214,000 more vehicles in November and December—roughly 107,000 a month—to reach the target, more than twice its October pace. The final October delivery figure had not yet been released.

business.title: Australian central bank set to raise rates again as home prices fall
business.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is widely expected to raise its cash rate by 0.25 percentage point on Tuesday, Nov. 3, to 4.85%, an 18-year high and its fifth increase this year. Its preferred measure of underlying inflation rose 1% in the September quarter, above the bank’s 0.8% forecast, while annual underlying i
business.content: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is widely expected to raise its cash rate by 0.25 percentage point on Tuesday, Nov. 3, to 4.85%, an 18-year high and its fifth increase this year. Its preferred measure of underlying inflation rose 1% in the September quarter, above the bank’s 0.8% forecast, while annual underlying inflation reached 3.7%. The increase would add pressure to a housing market facing falling prices, reduced borrowing capacity and strained affordability. National home values fell 1.1% in September. The bank will announce its decision at 2:30 p.m. Tuesday, followed an hour later by a news conference with Governor Michele Bullock. It will also release updated economic forecasts.
business.image_alt: Australian central bank set to raise rates again as home prices fall

business.title: Alphabet
business.summary: Alphabet spent $51.4 billion on capital projects in the third quarter of 2026, more than twice the year-earlier amount, and maintained its 2026 spending forecast of $195 billion to $205 billion while saying investment will rise significantly in 2027. Alphabet’s free cash flow fell to negative $9.1 billion from positive
business.content: Alphabet spent $51.4 billion on capital projects in the third quarter of 2026, more than twice the year-earlier amount, and maintained its 2026 spending forecast of $195 billion to $205 billion while saying investment will rise significantly in 2027. Alphabet’s free cash flow fell to negative $9.1 billion from positive $24.5 billion a year earlier. Alphabet Chief Financial Officer Anat Ashkenazi said the company expects returns on invested capital to remain meaningfully above its cost of capital. Free cash flow is expected to decline again in 2027 as spending increases. Google Cloud revenue grew 103% in the quarter.

business.title: AI spending worries drive mixed Asian trading before tech earnings
business.summary: Asian stocks were mixed on Monday, Nov. 2, as investors weighed concerns over artificial-intelligence spending against a rebound in U.S. futures ahead of a week of technology earnings. Japanese and Australian stocks fell, while South Korean and Hong Kong stocks gained; the MSCI Asia-Pacific index outside Japan slipped
business.content: Asian stocks were mixed on Monday, Nov. 2, as investors weighed concerns over artificial-intelligence spending against a rebound in U.S. futures ahead of a week of technology earnings. Japanese and Australian stocks fell, while South Korean and Hong Kong stocks gained; the MSCI Asia-Pacific index outside Japan slipped 0.4%. The moves followed Friday’s 3.5% drop in the Nasdaq 100 and a 7.2% decline in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, as worries about the scale and returns of AI investment weighed on technology shares. Apple, AMD and Palantir were due to report this week, with investors looking for evidence that earnings can support continued spending.
business.image_alt: AI spending worries drive mixed Asian trading before tech earnings

business.title: India factory growth eases to 54.7 as export orders accelerate
business.summary: India’s manufacturing growth slowed in October, with the HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI), compiled by S&P Global, easing to 54.7 from 55.1 in September. The reading remained above 50, the level separating expansion from contraction. New orders eased marginally from September’s seven-month high
business.content: India’s manufacturing growth slowed in October, with the HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI), compiled by S&P Global, easing to 54.7 from 55.1 in September. The reading remained above 50, the level separating expansion from contraction. New orders eased marginally from September’s seven-month high, and hiring growth slowed; capital-goods makers cut staff. Export orders rose at their fastest pace in six months, while factory output growth moderated. Manufacturers increased finished-goods inventories at a record pace in the survey’s more than 21-year history, while growth in raw-material purchasing slowed to its weakest in 64 months of expansion. Input-cost inflation fell to its lowest since February, and selling-price increases were the weakest in nearly four years. Business confidence remained below its long-run average.
business.image_alt: India factory growth eases to 54.7 as export orders accelerate

business.title: California voters decide whether to impose one-time 5% billionaire tax
business.summary: California voters will decide Tuesday, Nov. 3, whether to approve Proposition 40, which would impose a one-time 5% tax on the state’s billionaires, with most proceeds earmarked for health care and some for education and food assistance. If approved, it would be the first wealth tax in the modern United States. The meas
business.content: California voters will decide Tuesday, Nov. 3, whether to approve Proposition 40, which would impose a one-time 5% tax on the state’s billionaires, with most proceeds earmarked for health care and some for education and food assistance. If approved, it would be the first wealth tax in the modern United States. The measure’s backers say it would help offset federal health-care cuts; opponents warn that wealthy residents and investment could leave the state. More than 70 current and former California billionaires contributed $612 million to state election causes this year. Opponents of Proposition 40 alone raised more than $340 million, compared with just under $33 million for its supporters. Two rival ballot measures, Propositions 41 and 42, could block the tax if they receive more yes votes than Proposition 40, even if it passes.
business.image_alt: California voters decide whether to impose one-time 5% billionaire tax

science.title: Early outer Solar System bodies formed mostly from rock, study finds
science.summary: Bodies that formed in the outer Solar System during its first million years consisted of 83% to 92% chondrules—rock fragments created by intense heat—with little icy dust, an international team reports in Nature Astronomy. The study examined the composition of the earliest planetesimals, the building blocks of planets
science.content: Bodies that formed in the outer Solar System during its first million years consisted of 83% to 92% chondrules—rock fragments created by intense heat—with little icy dust, an international team reports in Nature Astronomy. The study examined the composition of the earliest planetesimals, the building blocks of planets and moons. The researchers inferred the mix from iron meteorites that preserve chemical traces of their parent bodies. They found more ice in bodies that formed later, consistent with a shift toward icy material after about two million years.
science.image_alt: Early outer Solar System bodies formed mostly from rock, study finds

science.title: Study finds fluent chatbots can win trust despite factual errors
science.summary: Researchers at Radboud University found that users rated a fluent chatbot giving false answers as just as intelligent and pleasant as a terse chatbot giving correct answers. In a test about The Lord of the Rings, 80% of participants missed errors despite having basic knowledge of the subject. Hikers who used Google’s G
science.content: Researchers at Radboud University found that users rated a fluent chatbot giving false answers as just as intelligent and pleasant as a terse chatbot giving correct answers. In a test about The Lord of the Rings, 80% of participants missed errors despite having basic knowledge of the subject. Hikers who used Google’s Gemini chatbot to plan a Mount Shasta trip later needed help, and a teenager rescued in British Columbia had used Anthropic’s Claude during trip planning. A separate research team has released DialFork, a benchmark designed to detect when conversational agents depart from the intended process even when their individual statements sound plausible. It contains 36,278 dialogues across 24 tasks and 12 domains.
science.image_alt: Study finds fluent chatbots can win trust despite factual errors

science.title: UN-backed report warns overshooting 1.5C could permanently damage Earth
science.summary: A report by 80 scientists convened by the International Cryosphere Climate Initiative and the U.N. Environment Programme warns that even a temporary rise above the Paris Agreement’s 1.5C warming limit could cause lasting losses to glaciers, sea ice and polar ice sheets. Earth has already warmed about 1.3C from preindus
science.content: A report by 80 scientists convened by the International Cryosphere Climate Initiative and the U.N. Environment Programme warns that even a temporary rise above the Paris Agreement’s 1.5C warming limit could cause lasting losses to glaciers, sea ice and polar ice sheets. Earth has already warmed about 1.3C from preindustrial levels. The authors say any period above 1.5C should be as brief as possible before temperatures fall much further, and identify a long-term target below 1C by 2150. Under current policies, warming is projected to reach about 2.8C, a level the report links to near-total thaw of near-surface permafrost and likely severe disruption to ocean circulation. Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets would continue losing ice even if temperatures later returned to 1.5C, while many ice systems could take centuries or millennia to recover. The report was released ahead of the COP31 climate conference in Turkey.
science.image_alt: UN-backed report warns overshooting 1.5C could permanently damage Earth

science.title: NASA Swift telescope faces uncontrolled reentry after failed orbit rescue
science.summary: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory is expected to reenter Earth’s atmosphere in the coming days after a failed attempt to raise its orbit. Forecasts place reentry roughly between Nov. 3 and Nov. 6, but the timing and location remain uncertain. The U.S. Space Force is tracking the 1.5-ton spacecraft. Most of it is ex
science.content: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory is expected to reenter Earth’s atmosphere in the coming days after a failed attempt to raise its orbit. Forecasts place reentry roughly between Nov. 3 and Nov. 6, but the timing and location remain uncertain. The U.S. Space Force is tracking the 1.5-ton spacecraft. Most of it is expected to burn up, although some dense tungsten components and mirror parts could survive. The possible reentry corridor spans a broad band near the equator, much of it over ocean. Solar activity increased atmospheric drag and accelerated the telescope’s orbital decline. Swift, launched in 2004 for a two-year mission, detected more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and 1,400 exploding stars and rapidly alerted other observatories to transient events. It continued observations after the rescue attempt was abandoned, but NASA shut down its systems in late October when its low orbit made stable operations impossible.
science.image_alt: NASA Swift telescope faces uncontrolled reentry after failed orbit rescue

science.title: Rubin observatory team finds possible dwarf planet in archived images
science.summary: A team led by University of Washington astronomer Mario Juric has identified a possible dwarf planet in early data from Chile’s Vera C. Rubin Observatory and estimates it is 1,000 to 2,000 miles across. The object, provisionally designated 2026 ED-138, lies about 46 astronomical units from Earth; the team also found it
science.content: A team led by University of Washington astronomer Mario Juric has identified a possible dwarf planet in early data from Chile’s Vera C. Rubin Observatory and estimates it is 1,000 to 2,000 miles across. The object, provisionally designated 2026 ED-138, lies about 46 astronomical units from Earth; the team also found it in older observations, including photographic plates dating to the 1930s. The estimated size would make it far larger than the asteroids the survey team usually detects, but astronomers have not established that it is round, a requirement for dwarf-planet status. Because it is too distant for researchers to image its shape directly, they plan to study how it dims stars as it passes in front of them; one such event may occur within days, Juric said. He expects confirmation to take about two years.
science.image_alt: Rubin observatory team finds possible dwarf planet in archived images

sports.title: Manchester United keep Carrick for two matches before reviewing his future
sports.summary: Manchester United will keep head coach Michael Carrick in charge for Tuesday’s Champions League match against Roma and Sunday’s Premier League game against Aston Villa, then reassess his position during the November international break. The decision follows Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, which extended United’s winl
sports.content: Manchester United will keep head coach Michael Carrick in charge for Tuesday’s Champions League match against Roma and Sunday’s Premier League game against Aston Villa, then reassess his position during the November international break. The decision follows Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, which extended United’s winless run to nine matches in all competitions and left them 17th in the Premier League on seven points, above the relegation zone only on goal difference. United had already discussed Carrick’s future after losing 3-0 at home to Bournemouth, but club leaders decided to give him more time. Reports identify former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann as possible successors. The Guardian reported contact with both camps, while VnExpress, citing journalist David Ornstein, said United had not directly approached replacements. United host Roma on November 3 and Villa on November 8, before the break begins on November 9. Lisandro Martínez will miss the Villa game through suspension.
sports.image_alt: Manchester United keep Carrick for two matches before reviewing his future

sports.title: Falkirk end 19-year Celtic drought with 2-0 Scottish Premiership win
sports.summary: Falkirk beat Scottish champions Celtic 2-0 on Sunday, ending a wait of nearly 20 years for a win over the Glasgow side. Ethan Ross scored in the third minute after Cameron Carter-Vickers misplayed a cross, and Scott Tanser doubled Falkirk’s lead in the 38th minute. Former Celtic goalkeeper Scott Bain made 10 saves as F
sports.content: Falkirk beat Scottish champions Celtic 2-0 on Sunday, ending a wait of nearly 20 years for a win over the Glasgow side. Ethan Ross scored in the third minute after Cameron Carter-Vickers misplayed a cross, and Scott Tanser doubled Falkirk’s lead in the 38th minute. Former Celtic goalkeeper Scott Bain made 10 saves as Falkirk held on. A second-half goal was disallowed for handball after a video review. The loss denied Celtic a chance to extend their lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership to seven points. They remain four points ahead of Rangers but have played one more match. Sunday’s result was their sixth defeat in 10 games in all competitions. Falkirk climbed to fourth with a fourth straight league win. Celtic manager Martin O’Neill said his team must improve their defending, but also pointed to missed chances and Bain’s performance. Celtic next host Besiktas in the Europa League on Thursday, November 5, after losing their first three matches in the competition.
sports.image_alt: Falkirk end 19-year Celtic drought with 2-0 Scottish Premiership win

sports.title: Real Madrid beat Racing 3-0 as China broadcast blackout continues
sports.summary: Real Madrid beat Racing Santander 3-0 on Sunday, Nov. 1, with Kylian Mbappé scoring an 11th-minute penalty before Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomandé added first-half goals. The win extended Madrid’s run to six victories across all competitions and left manager José Mourinho’s side third in La Liga, three points behind le
sports.content: Real Madrid beat Racing Santander 3-0 on Sunday, Nov. 1, with Kylian Mbappé scoring an 11th-minute penalty before Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomandé added first-half goals. The win extended Madrid’s run to six victories across all competitions and left manager José Mourinho’s side third in La Liga, three points behind leaders Barcelona and one behind Atlético Madrid. Chinese broadcasters continued to withhold Spanish league matches after Mbappé apologized for remarks about a meme depicting him as Mao Zedong. State broadcaster CCTV showed no La Liga games over the weekend; streaming service Migu carried most other fixtures but not Madrid’s, while several Chinese companies ended commercial deals with the French forward. China Media Group acknowledged the apologies from Mbappé, Madrid and La Liga but has not said when broadcasts may resume. Madrid are scheduled to visit AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday. At the time of reporting, Chinese rights-holder iQiyi Sports’ schedule did not list the match.
sports.image_alt: Real Madrid beat Racing 3-0 as China broadcast blackout continues

sports.title: Andrew Novak claims first solo PGA Tour title with Mexico Open win
sports.summary: Andrew Novak won the VidantaWorld Mexico Open in Vallarta, Mexico, by five strokes on Sunday, finishing at a tournament-record 25-under 259 for his first individual PGA Tour title. He closed with a two-under 69, making three consecutive birdies on holes 12 through 14 after his lead had narrowed to three shots. Novak pr
sports.content: Andrew Novak won the VidantaWorld Mexico Open in Vallarta, Mexico, by five strokes on Sunday, finishing at a tournament-record 25-under 259 for his first individual PGA Tour title. He closed with a two-under 69, making three consecutive birdies on holes 12 through 14 after his lead had narrowed to three shots. Novak previously won the 2025 Zurich Classic with Ben Griffin. His individual victory moved him from 89th to 53rd in the FedEx Cup Fall standings in the race for places in next season’s $20 million signature events. The Mexico Open ran Oct. 29-Nov. 1; the next PGA Tour event in Mexico, the World Wide Technology Championship, is scheduled for Nov. 5-8 in Los Cabos.
sports.image_alt: Andrew Novak claims first solo PGA Tour title with Mexico Open win

sports.title: Broncos rally past Chiefs 28-24 to take AFC West lead
sports.summary: The Denver Broncos erased an 11-point deficit to beat the Kansas City Chiefs 28-24 on Sunday, Nov. 1, moving to 6-2 and into first place in the AFC West, a half-game ahead of the 5-2 Chiefs. sports.content: The Denver Broncos erased an 11-point deficit to beat the Kansas City Chiefs 28-24 on Sunday, Nov. 1, moving to 6-2 and into first place in the AFC West, a half-game ahead of the 5-2 Chiefs. Denver scored 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, then stopped Kansas City at the 1-yard line: a false-start penalty erased a potential Rashee Rice touchdown, and defensive tackle Malcolm Roach sacked Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes on the final play. After Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal with 2½ minutes left, Denver scored the go-ahead touchdown on its next two plays: a 51-yard reception by rookie Jonah Coleman followed by his 5-yard score. Kansas City’s loss was its second in a row. The Chiefs host the New York Jets next Sunday, while Denver visits the Carolina Panthers.

sports.content: New Zealand beat India by seven wickets in the fifth T20 International in Hamilton on November 1, chasing 192 with 12 balls to spare, but India won the five-match series 3-2 after winning the first three games. Tim Seifert struck 93 from 50 balls and Glenn Phillips finished unbeaten on 65 as New Zealand reached 195-3. Earlier, Ishan Kishan made 61 and India captain Shreyas Iyer scored 50, but Adam Milne took four wickets to help restrict India to 191-8. Phillips scored 341 runs in the series, a record for a batter in a bilateral men’s T20I series, surpassing Phil Salt’s 331 for England against the West Indies in 2023. New Zealand won the final two matches after India had secured the series. Iyer said India needed to improve its bowling and fielding, while head coach Gautam Gambhir praised the team for adapting to unfamiliar conditions after only one day of practice. The teams begin a five-match one-day international series at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday, November 4.

sports.content: Spain’s Carlos Alcaraz beat Australia’s Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 in 87 minutes on Sunday to win the Vienna Open, his fourth title of 2026 and 28th of his career. Alcaraz did not drop a set during the tournament and extended his unbeaten run at ATP 500 events to 26 matches. Alcaraz broke De Minaur early and controlled the first set. The Australian kept the second set closer but conceded the decisive break in the final game. De Minaur reached the final by beating Alexander Zverev in a three-set semifinal, while Alcaraz defeated Daniil Medvedev. Zverev is set to take the world No. 1 ranking on Monday, November 2. Alcaraz returned at the US Open after a wrist injury kept him out for almost five months, then won in Tokyo before arriving in Austria. He has already qualified for the ATP Finals in Turin, while De Minaur heads to the Paris Masters still seeking a place in the season-ending event.

sports.content: Sweden’s Andreas Almgren won the men’s race at the New York City Marathon on Sunday, November 1, in 2:06:01 in his debut over the 26.2-mile distance. He pulled away from Italy’s Yemaneberhan Crippa in the final mile; Lesotho’s Kamohelo Mofolo took third, one second ahead of defending champion Benson Kipruto. Almgren’s time was the third-fastest in the course’s 50-year history, and he became the first marathon debutant to win the race since 2010. Kenya’s Sheila Chepkirui won the women’s race in 2:24:36 for her second New York title, following her 2024 victory. She held off compatriot Hellen Obiri, the defending champion. American Jessica McClain passed Obiri late to finish second, six seconds behind Chepkirui and one second ahead of Obiri. Swiss racers swept the wheelchair events: Marcel Hug secured his eighth men’s title in a sprint finish, and Catherine Debrunner won the women’s race. Around 60,000 runners took part in the 50th running of the five-borough course.
